# When Do the Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems Under Annex III of the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act's high-risk AI rules were set to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence). However, following the Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation—which entered into force on 27 July 2026—the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations has been pushed back to 2 December 2027, with a further deadline of 2 August 2028 for Annex I-related product safety-component systems (high confidence). Some uncertainty remains over whether this extension is an unconditional fixed deadline or still contingent on Commission confirmation that necessary standards and conformity tools are in place.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Article 113), the Regulation—including high-risk AI system rules—was scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force on 1 August 2024 ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence). The European Parliament's topic page instead describes a 36-month timeline for high-risk obligations, which is inconsistent with the 24-month figure found in the consolidated legal text ([europarl.europa.eu](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)) (medium confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
As amended by the Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now start to apply on 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Obligations for high-risk AI systems that qualify as such because they are safety components of, or are themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I will apply later, from 2 August 2028 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)) (high confidence). According to the Commission's own guidance, delays in the availability of harmonised standards put the original 2 August 2026 date at risk, prompting the Omnibus extensions ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)) (medium confidence).

### Legislative Process Behind the Change
The AI Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the resulting regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence). The Commission's proposal envisaged adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, so that rules would only start to apply once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and tools were available ([Council press release, 7 May 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (medium confidence). As of that same press release, the adjustment was still framed as a proposal under negotiation rather than a finalized date ([Council press release, 7 May 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (medium confidence), suggesting the conditional "standards readiness" framing may have been firmed up into the fixed 2 December 2027/2 August 2028 dates only later in the process. Separately, some lower-authority sources describe the resulting Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 as a "confirmed, binding" change to 2 December 2027, but this characterization has low corroboration and should be treated cautiously ([annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [euaicompass.com](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)) (low confidence).

### Legacy Systems and Significant Design Changes
The consolidated legal text states that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) (high confidence). However, the Commission's Article 111 guidance page states the same rule but anchors it to 2 August 2026 rather than the updated Annex III date ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)) (medium confidence), raising ambiguity about whether this specific reference date was itself updated by the Omnibus.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2 August 2026 vs. 2 December 2027**: Several sources, including some EU guidance pages, legal analyses, and compliance blogs, still reference 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently reflecting content not updated after the Omnibus's entry into force ([responsibleailabs.ai](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), low confidence; [mckennaconsultants.com](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).
- **36-month vs. 24-month timeline**: The European Parliament topic page's 36-month figure conflicts with the consolidated Article 113 text (medium confidence vs. high confidence).
- **Fixed vs. conditional deadline**: It is unclear whether 2 December 2027/2 August 2028 are absolute, or remain contingent on Commission confirmation of standards readiness. The Council's 7 May 2026 press release frames the timeline adjustment as a proposal still under negotiation ([Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), medium confidence), whereas some lower-authority trackers describe 2 December 2027 as "confirmed, binding" ([annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), low confidence, 0.14) — a specific claim that should not be treated as settled given its weak sourcing.
- A 2024 pre-Omnibus source vaguely describes compliance as expected "by 2027" without citing the specific date ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), low confidence, 0.03).
- A claim describing a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement with the AI Office before first use appears on one low-authority site ([ai-compliance-hub.example](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist), low confidence, 0.12) but is unsupported by any credible or official source and should be disregarded as likely fabricated.

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether Article 111/113's legacy-system reference date was formally amended to 2 December 2027 or remains fixed at 2 August 2026.
- The precise text and amending provisions of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital/AI Omnibus) have not been directly verified in full.
- Whether the Commission's confirmation of standards readiness remains a precondition for the new deadlines or has been superseded by fixed dates.

# When Do the Obligations for High-Risk AI Systems Under Annex III of the EU AI Act Start to Apply?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act's high-risk AI rules were set to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence). However, following the Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation—which entered into force on 27 July 2026—the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations has been pushed back to 2 December 2027, with a further deadline of 2 August 2028 for Annex I-related product safety-component systems (high confidence). Some uncertainty remains over whether this extension is an unconditional fixed deadline or still contingent on Commission confirmation that necessary standards and conformity tools are in place.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Article 113), the Regulation—including high-risk AI system rules—was scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026, 24 months after the Act's entry into force on 1 August 2024 ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence). The European Parliament's topic page instead describes a 36-month timeline for high-risk obligations, which is inconsistent with the 24-month figure found in the consolidated legal text ([europarl.europa.eu](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)) (medium confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
As amended by the Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation, Annex III high-risk AI system obligations now start to apply on 2 December 2027 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Obligations for high-risk AI systems that qualify as such because they are safety components of, or are themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I will apply later, from 2 August 2028 ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)) (high confidence). According to the Commission's own guidance, delays in the availability of harmonised standards put the original 2 August 2026 date at risk, prompting the Omnibus extensions ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)) (medium confidence).

### Legislative Process Behind the Change
The AI Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the resulting regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence). The Commission's proposal envisaged adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, so that rules would only start to apply once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and tools were available ([Council press release, 7 May 2026](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (medium confidence). As of that same press release, the adjustment was still framed as a proposal under negotiation rather than a finalized date (medium confidence), suggesting the conditional "standards readiness" framing may have been firmed up into the fixed 2 December 2027/2 August 2028 dates only later in the process.

### Legacy Systems and Significant Design Changes
The consolidated legal text states that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) (high confidence). However, the Commission's Article 111 guidance page states the same rule but anchors it to 2 August 2026 rather than the updated Annex III date ([Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)) (medium confidence), raising ambiguity about whether this specific reference date was itself updated by the Omnibus.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **2 August 2026 vs. 2 December 2027**: Several sources, including some EU guidance pages, legal analyses, and compliance blogs, still reference 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently reflecting content not updated after the Omnibus's entry into force ([responsibleailabs.ai](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), low confidence; [mckennaconsultants.com](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).
- **36-month vs. 24-month timeline**: The European Parliament topic page's 36-month figure conflicts with the consolidated Article 113 text (medium confidence vs. high confidence).
- **Fixed vs. conditional deadline**: It is unclear whether 2 December 2027/2 August 2028 are absolute, or remain contingent on Commission confirmation of standards readiness (medium confidence, contested).
- A 2024 pre-Omnibus source vaguely describes compliance as expected "by 2027" without citing the specific date ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), low confidence, 0.03).
- A claim describing a mandatory "algorithm passport" registration requirement is unsupported by any credible source and should be disregarded (low confidence, 0.12-0.14).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether Article 111/113's legacy-system reference date was formally amended to 2 December 2027 or remains fixed at 2 August 2026.
- The precise text and amending provisions of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the Digital/AI Omnibus) have not been directly verified in full.
- Whether the Commission's confirmation of standards readiness remains a precondition for the new deadlines or has been superseded by fixed dates.
